newsitem.title: UK: UK construction orders up 4.0 pct in 3mths to Nov.
newsitem.headline: UK construction orders up 4.0 pct in 3mths to Nov.

text.p: UK new construction orders rose 4.0 percent in the three months to November compared with the previous three months, and were 5.0 percent higher compared with the same three months in 1995, the Department of the Environment said on Tuesday.

New orders in the private housing sector in the three months to November were 30 percent higher compared with the previous three months and 34 percent higher than in the corresponding period a year ago.

Public housing and housing association orders in the latest three months were 25 percent lower than in the previous three months and 16 percent lower than in the same period a year earlier, the DOE said.
Infrastructure orders in the latest three months were two percent higher compared with the previous three months and 11 percent higher compared with the corresponding period a year earlier.

Public non-housing orders (excluding infrastructure) in the latest three months were unchanged compared with the previous three months but seven percent lower than in the corresponding period a year ago.
Private industrial orders in the latest three months were 16 percent higher than in the previous three months but 14 percent lower compared with the same period a year ago.
Private commercial orders in the latest three months were 11 percent lower compared with the previous three months and two percent lower than in the corresponding period a year ago.
The DOE said the level of overall new contruction orders was at its highest level for nearly a year.

"This was mainly due to private housing having its best performance since 1989 and infrastructure recording a high in 1996 -- the latter resulting from a number of large Private Finance Initiative roads contracts," it said in a statement.
